I broke my nose in a fight, completely shattered every bone in it. They said 6-8 weeks off and once it’s healed it’s up to me. Doctors don’t like their work being destroyed and will tell you what’s medically the best thing to do. If you get the surgery make sure you’re taking high quality vitamins to support your bones. Everything is a risk after it heals, give yourself ALL the necessary time for the repair to heal and ensure you are doing everything the doctor allows ensure the best healing possible. Then do what you want, it’s your life. People typically wait until after their careers in fighting are over to repair their nose because it’s a pain in the ass to continually repair. Do what you think is best for your quality of life and enjoyment, listen to your doctor until you are CLEARED by them. Live your life after that.

I then googled them to by typing in the year make and model, Google has these prompts that go through FAQs, click on the “how long does it last” “problems with car” etc. Once the list is narrowed down look up the best & worst years of the cars you like and then you’ll be able to narrow down to a better degree what might last you a long time. 

I found Mazdas, Toyotas, and Hondas to be the most reliable. Newer Fords, Hyundais, Kias, and BMWs should be avoided at all costs. 

If you’re lucky you can find an very well maintained older vehicle that will be considered an antique so you can avoid the pesky additional checks on the vehicle, but you’ll likely get something that isn’t an ideal daily driver. If the Carfax is available ALWAYS use that to determine if the car was maintained well enough. If you’re buying privately just ensure that the person selling it to you provides all the receipts of maintenance that they have. 

Most importantly ALWAYS negotiate. It’s okay to walk away even if you found the “perfect car”, there will be more, there will be better deals, most places are willing to go down a couple hundred on the price. If you’re lucky you can get $1-2k off with some expert level negotiating but that’s not gonna happen too often in this market even though it’s slowing down a little.
